description: ParaEMT is an open electromagnetic-transient simulator for inverter-rich power networks published by the national laboratory developers. Python and Numba code solves nodal network equations with trapezoidal integration and updates device states. The repository documents result down-sampling, saved simulation snapshots and test systems ranging from the Kundur two-area case to WECC 179- and 240-bus systems. Inputs include solved power-flow JSON files and device models; outputs are transient trajectories and restart snapshots. These are benchmark and user-configured networks, not a current inventory of the Western grid. Source and workflow documentation are public and free under BSD-3-Clause, with Python 3.7 or newer specified. A critical limitation is that the README says BBD parallel simulation was disabled because nxmetis is unmaintained. Several additional functions and a manual are described as forthcoming and are not treated here as available capabilities. The simulator supports fault and dynamic-response studies alongside steady-state tools such as pandapower (model-pandapower). Published benchmark claims were not reproduced, and no test-system archive was downloaded.
name: ParaEMT electromagnetic-transient simulator
